\subsection{The type of a varargs parameter}
\seclabel{revival-varargs}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{function-decls}.
\item[Change] A box after the sentence of \secref{function-decls} that gives a
varargs parameter the type \EXP{\TYP{HeapSequence}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}
says that no library declares that type, nor the immutable sequence that the
team's draft note at the start of \secref{function-app} agreed on in its place;
that both implementations give the parameter the array type
\EXP{\TYP{ImmutableArray}\llbracket{}T, \mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket} of \library;
and that the compiled path's own library declares no such type.
The normative text is unchanged.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 23~September 2026 that the implementers' later word
outweighs text that the designers left unfinished.
The text and its draft notes name \TYP{HeapSequence} and
\TYP{ReadOnlyHeapSequence} (``We agreed to implement varargs tuples using
\TYP{ReadOnlyHeapSequence} which is immutable and invariant.
We'll add \TYP{MakeReadOnlyHeapSequence} into the core library.''), and no
library declares either.
The authors of the compiled type checker named a type for the parameter,
\EXP{\TYP{ImmutableArray}\llbracket{}T, \mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket}, with the
comment ``Replace ImmutableArray with ImmutableHeapSequence when
ImmutableHeapSequence is put into the libraries''
(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Types.java}, lines
47--49, in the revival's repository), and the interpreter binds the parameter
to an immutable one-dimensional array of the arguments that the factory
\VAR{\_\_immutableFactory1} of \library\ builds
(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/NonPrimitive.java},
lines 224--251), a value of that type.
The type is immutable, as the draft note asks.
Before this change the compiled type checker typed the parameter in the body
as \VAR{T}, the type of one argument, and read a parameter list with plain
bindings before a varargs binding as if the varargs binding were one more plain
binding, so that a call that passed no argument, or more than one, for the
varargs binding after plain bindings was refused (row~604 of the revival's gap
ledger).
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-defects/REPORT.md} in the
revival's repository.
\item[Effect] The compiled type checker applies a declaration with a varargs
parameter to a call as \secref{function-app} and
\secref{applicability-with-special-params} say, whatever the number of
arguments for the varargs binding, none among them, each a subtype of the type
of the binding or convertible to it; and it types the parameter in the body at
\EXP{\TYP{ImmutableArray}\llbracket{}T, \mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket} of \library,
where it typed it as \VAR{T}.
Under the compiled path's own library, which declares no \TYP{ImmutableArray},
it refuses every use of a varargs parameter, in a body, a contract or a
function expression, naming the type.
There the code generator refuses a function with a varargs parameter, naming
the type.
Against \library, the code generator passes the arguments that no plain
binding takes as one array of that type, which the factory
\VAR{\_\_immutableFactory1} makes and the caller fills in order, at the call
or, where another declaration of the name takes as many arguments, in the
dispatch method's branch for the varargs declaration; a program compiled
against \library\ does not run yet, so no program with a varargs parameter
runs on the compiled path.
Neither implementation passes the elements of a spread argument,
\EXP{f(1, \VAR{xs}\ldots)}, to the parameter: each calls the declaration
without them (row~1085 of the revival's gap ledger).
The code generator does not yet compile a varargs declaration that is a
method of a trait or object, or that has static parameters, beside another
declaration of its name that takes as many parameters (row~1086 of the
revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter is unchanged.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/functions.tex},
lines 178--180, which stand unchanged and are now followed, after the draft
note that refers to the library section for \TYP{HeapSequence}, by the box:
\begin{quote}
The type of a varargs parameter
is \EXP{\TYP{HeapSequence}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket} where \VAR{T} is
the type mentioned in (or inferred for) that binding.
\end{quote}

    Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652); the code

    (row~11).

The review is right on each of these:

- The rule. - The code. - The omission. G's report lists three sentences made false or checked (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-varargs/REPORT.md:131-133`), and not this one; the gather's record names only `preamble.tex:84` as left to it (`RECORD.md:169`).

The review's suggested clause is right in substance and I keep it, with two changes of form: it names, beside the refusal, that against the one library the code generator compiles one, which is what row 624's close records; and it points to `\secref{revival-varargs}` (`changes.tex:3996`), whose Effect names the forms still not compiled (row 1086) and the spread argument that neither implementation passes (row 1085), instead of repeating them.

    \revision{revival-supported}{The Working Draft said that keyword parameters and
    variable size argument lists are supported.
    Keyword parameters are not built, and compiled code takes no variable size
    argument list.}

A callout "says what walk or the compiled path does" (`references/records.md`, "Sentences of the specification made false"), so it is corrected in the same repair. The sentence of the introduction itself, "Variable size argument lists are also supported under the interpreter" (`nutshell.tex:106-107`), and the team's note at `nutshell.tex:14-15` stay.

## No other finding

- The review's corrections commit, `17b55bcc72`, changes only paths under `explorations/` (`git show --stat 17b55bcc72`: twelve files, all under `explorations/`).
- The batch's other edits under `Specification/` are G's (`git diff --stat c799851472 HEAD -- Specification`: `changes.tex`, 18 lines, and `functions.tex`, 9 lines), which the review checked and the gather built ('Output written on fortress.pdf (727 pages, 2533509 bytes)', `RECORD.md:53`).

       Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652).
       The code generator refuses a varargs parameter under the compiled path's own
       library, which declares no \TYP{ImmutableArray}; against \library\ it compiles
       one, but a program compiled against \library\ does not run yet (row~1062), and
       \secref{revival-varargs} names the forms that it does not yet compile.
       An object takes no varargs parameter (row~11).

   `\TYP` is used so at `changes.tex:4043`, `\library` is defined in `Specification/latex-common/macros/macros.tex:78`, and `revival-varargs` is the label at `changes.tex:3996`. Change nothing else of the entry: its Rationale's count of items (`:6385-6386`) and the preface's list are unchanged, since the preface's item stays.

2. In `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:110-111`, replace

       Keyword parameters are not built, and compiled code takes no variable size
       argument list.}

   with

       Keyword parameters are not built, and no program with a variable size argument
       list runs on the compiled path yet.}

   leaving `:108-109` as they are.

3. Check that no sentence of the specification still cites row 624: `grep -rn '~624' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing.

With `pdftotext`, quote the new Effect sentence and the new callout from the built PDF. Then `git clean -fXq -- Specification`. Do not update `Specification/fortress.pdf`. Build nothing under `ProjectFortress/` and run no test: no code changes, and an edit of the specification has no test (`SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task").

5.
